entry_point.discipline_context: Use equilibrium and curvature as familiar entry points, then connect them to numerical relaxation without equating optimisation with physical dynamics.
entry_point.rationale: The learner knows potential energy, vectors, matrices, eigenvalues, and Python but not formal convex optimisation.
entry_point.analogy_boundary: Potential energy and equilibrium motivate intuition only: an objective may be an error or cost, and an iteration index is an algorithmic label rather than physical time.

conditional_item_decisions.rationale: Exact line search is explicitly required in the fixed scope.
Armijo backtracking is explicitly required in the fixed scope.
Heavy Ball is explicitly required in the fixed scope.
The quadratic Heavy Ball parameter result is explicitly required.
The specified NAG recurrence is explicitly required.
The convex NAG rate is explicitly required.
The finite-sum stochastic model and variance assumptions are explicitly required.
The SGD update and constant-step error floor are explicitly required.
Newton's second-order model is explicitly required.
The Newton linear-system step is explicitly required.
Newton local convergence conditions are explicitly required.
BFGS vectors and secant equation are explicitly required.
The BFGS update, curvature condition, direction, and line search are explicitly required.

chapter_sequence.title: Equilibrium, stationarity, and curvature
chapter_sequence.purpose: Introduce unconstrained objectives and separate necessary from sufficient local conditions.

chapter_sequence.title: Smoothness, convexity, and conditioning
chapter_sequence.purpose: Build the global geometric vocabulary used by convergence theorems.

chapter_sequence.title: Gradient descent and step selection
chapter_sequence.purpose: Derive the basic update and compare constant, exact, and Armijo steps.

chapter_sequence.title: What gradient descent guarantees
chapter_sequence.purpose: State convex and strongly convex rates with their matching assumptions and steps.

chapter_sequence.title: Momentum and acceleration
chapter_sequence.purpose: Distinguish Heavy Ball from NAG and state their bounded results.

chapter_sequence.title: Stochastic gradients and adaptive scaling
chapter_sequence.purpose: Move from finite-sum sampling to SGD, diminishing steps, and element-wise adaptive methods.

chapter_sequence.title: Second-order and quasi-Newton methods
chapter_sequence.purpose: Use curvature models for Newton and approximate curvature for BFGS.

chapter_sequence.title: From updates to Python operations
chapter_sequence.purpose: Make vector updates, objective values, and numerical behaviour explicit in executable Python.

chapter_sequence.title: Exercises and worked solutions
chapter_sequence.purpose: Check theorem scope, perform a hand update, and diagnose an implementation.

implementation_strategy: Use a pure-Python quadratic example so the gradient evaluation, subtraction, loop, and convergence output are visible without hiding operations in a library optimizer.
assessment_strategy: Use exactly three worked exercises: theorem-scope concept check, deterministic hand calculation with objective-gradient consistency, and code diagnostic with separate incorrect and corrected executable blocks.

exercise_plan.learning_objective: Identify which hypotheses make stationarity necessary or sufficient and which assumptions support a convergence statement.
exercise_plan.discipline_context: Classify an equilibrium-like stationary configuration in a numerical design objective without calling it automatically stable.

exercise_plan.learning_objective: Compute one gradient-descent update and check that the stated gradient matches its quadratic objective.
exercise_plan.discipline_context: Take one numerical relaxation step for a two-variable quadratic surrogate of a mechanical design cost.

exercise_plan.learning_objective: Locate a sign or gradient-evaluation error, then connect corrected Python output to descent behaviour.
exercise_plan.discipline_context: Diagnose a relaxation loop intended to reduce a scalar quadratic objective.
